title: Log smooth morphisms preserve log regularity
statement: Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Assume $f$ is log smooth in the chart sense [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] and $(Y,M_Y)$ is log regular in the stratum-and-dimension sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Then $(X,M_X)$ is log regular in that same sense. No injectivity or torsion-free-cokernel assumption on a prescribed chart is imposed beyond log smoothness. In particular this applies to a log smooth morphism over the spectrum of an arbitrary field [def-weil-field] equipped with its trivial log structure, since that log scheme is log regular.

source.place: Expose VI 1.8, printed p.70, the general log-smooth preservation statement, with reference to Kato 1994 Theorem 8.2 and its etale variant; also X Remark 1.1.1(b), printed p.136. No Stacks tag states this logarithmic assertion.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and choose chart neighbourhoods $X_0\to Y_0$ from [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], with monoid map $u:P\to Q$, smooth comparison and finite kernel $K=\ker u^{\rm gp}$. Work on these neighbourhoods. Their pulled-back log structures have the same geometric stalks as the original ones: pointed etale neighbourhoods form the same refining system. Thus log regularity of $Y$ gives log regularity of $Y_0$, and proving the defining regularity and dimension equality above each $\bar x$ suffices by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. If $N$ is the product of the orders of $K$ and of the torsion subgroup of the chart cokernel, its invertibility at $\bar x$ implies its invertibility at the image point of $Y_0$, since the residue fields embed. Restrict $Y_0$ to $D(N)$ and $X_0$ to its inverse image from the outset.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.2 and 1.8, pp.69--70; etale chart reduction.

proof.text: Every $k\in K$ is torsion in $P^{\rm gp}$; saturation puts both $k$ and $-k$ in $P$, so $K\subset P^\times$. Let $v_k=\alpha_Y(k)$, a unit on $Y_0$. Compatibility gives $f^*v_k=1$, hence $v_k=1$ in the residue field at the image of $\bar x$. If $d$ is the order of $k$, then $v_k^d=1$. The integer $d$ is invertible there, since it divides $|K|$, which is invertible at $\bar x$, and residue fields embed along $f$. In the factorization $(v_k-1)(1+v_k+\cdots+v_k^{d-1})=0$, the second factor has residue $d$, so it is invertible on an open neighbourhood. Therefore $v_k=1$ on that neighbourhood. Intersect these neighbourhoods for the finite group $K$ and restrict $X_0$ to its inverse image. All kernel elements now map to $1$ in the base log structure, because the log structure identifies its units with scheme units.

source.place: VI 1.8: explicit finite-kernel removal in the chart criterion.

proof.text: Put $R=P/K$, the image of $P$ in $P^{\rm gp}/K$. This is fs: finite generators descend; it embeds in its group completion; if $ng$ lies in $R$, lift $g$ to $P^{\rm gp}$, write $ng=p+k$, and use $k\in K\subset P$ and saturation of $P$ to put that lift in $P$. The chart factors through $R$, and its associated log structure is unchanged: the quotient relations identify only units $k$ already mapped to $1$. The mutually inverse stalk pushout maps send $[p,a]$ to $[\bar p,a]$ and conversely, as in [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. The map $h:R\to Q$ has injective group map and the same cokernel as $u^{\rm gp}$. Moreover $\mathbf Z[R]=\mathbf Z[P]/(z^k-1:k\in K)$. Since these relations already vanish on $Y_0$, the comparison target is unchanged on affine tensor rings. Thus the comparison is still smooth. This changes the chart, imposing no additional hypothesis on the original one.

source.place: VI 1.8, kernel-free chart reduction; associated-log stalk and monoid-ring quotient calculation.

proof.text: Let $Z=Y_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$, with its associated $Q$-log structure from [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. This is locally Noetherian: on any affine base chart its ring is $E\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], a finite-type $E$-algebra generated by finitely many $Q$-monomials; apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Fix any geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, with image $\bar y$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y_0,\bar y}$ and pull $Z$ back to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. At the lifted point its ordinary local ring is $B=(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q])_{\mathfrak q}$, with $\mathfrak q$ contracting to the maximal ideal of $A$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]; the tensor algebra and $B$ are Noetherian by finite type and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

Let $G=\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)$, $F=\{q\in Q:z^q\in B^\times\}$, $S=R_G/G^{\rm gp}$ and $T=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$. These are faces and their sharp quotients are fs by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. Since $A\to B$ is local, $h^{-1}F=G$. The chart-stalk formula [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] identifies the base characteristic with $S$ and the source characteristic with $T$; the nonunit ideal on $B$ is $J=(z^q:q\notin F)B$. Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] and [lem-trf-log-regular-completed-chart] to $Y_0$ at $\bar y$. Choose the permitted replacement of the sharp chart $a:S\to A$, so $\widehat A$ has its monomial-compatible equal- or mixed-characteristic presentation. The original chart on $R_G$ and $a$ lift the same characteristic: their ratio is a unique unit, by cancellation in the integral log stalk. Those ratios multiply, defining a character $\epsilon:R^{\rm gp}\to A^\times$ with $\alpha(r)=\epsilon(r)a(\bar r)$. This retains the unit twist in applying the completed model.

Apply [lem-sfb-completed-tame-monoid-base-change-model] to $A,R,Q,h,a,\epsilon$ of Steps 4--5. Its hypotheses hold without any Kummer condition or injectivity on sharp monoids. It identifies $(\widehat B,J\widehat B)$ with $(D[[T]],L)$ in equal characteristic, or $(D[[T]]/(\eta),L)$ in mixed characteristic, where $D$ is complete regular Noetherian local, $L$ is generated by the nonzero $T$-monomials and the reduction $\bar\eta$ is a regular parameter of $D$. The ring in question is nonzero since it is localized at the specified prime.

source.place: VI 1.6--1.8, p.70; agent-formulated completed monoid-base-change input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension]. If $e=0$ in the first case and $e=1$ in the second, it gives regularity of the quotient $D$ or $D/(\bar\eta)$ and the equalities $\dim\widehat B=\dim D+\operatorname{rank}T^{\rm gp}-e$ and $\dim(\widehat B/J\widehat B)=\dim D-e$. The latter quotient is the completion of $B/J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] give that $B/J$ is regular and $\dim B=\dim(B/J)+\operatorname{rank}T^{\rm gp}$.

The closed-immersion formula [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] gives $B^{\rm sh}/JB^{\rm sh}=(B/J)^{\rm sh}$. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] to the Noetherian rings $B,B/J$. Regularity of the quotient and the same dimension equality follow after strict henselization. By [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance], applied to the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y_0$, this $B^{\rm sh}$ is the geometric local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$. The identification is over $Z$, so preserves every $Q$-monomial and hence its nonunit ideal. Local maps reflect units, so the characteristic remains $T$. These are precisely the two conditions for log regularity in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. They hold at every $\bar z$, proving that $Z$ is log regular.

The comparison $c:X_0\to Z$ is strict: both log structures are associated to the identical $Q$-chart, and [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] identifies the pullback chart with the given source log structure. It is smooth by the original chart hypothesis and Step 3. Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to $c$ with the identical monoids $Q\xrightarrow{1}Q$. Its group map is injective with zero, hence torsion-free, cokernel; its comparison is $c$ itself and its target is log regular by Step 8. Its conclusion makes $X_0$ log regular. Step 1 then proves log regularity of $X$, with the empty source case vacuous.

For a field $F$ with trivial log structure, $F$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $F$. Its maximal ideal and Krull dimension are zero, so it is regular. Its geometric local rings are strict henselizations. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] these are regular of dimension zero. The nonunit log ideal is zero and the characteristic monoid and its rank are zero. Therefore the dimension equality is $0=0+0$, and [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] makes the trivial log field log regular. The result just proved applies over it, regardless of perfection of $F$.
